INTERPRETIVE CALL (flagged for audit, differs from the simpler pattern in the other cases in this eval set): Part III (10-14) does NOT use the classic 'each item independently reads incorporated by reference to the proxy' pattern seen in AAPL/MSFT/GE/Textron. Instead, a single consolidated incorporation-by-reference sentence ('Information to be provided in Items 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14 ... is incorporated by reference to the Firm's Definitive Proxy Statement ...') is embedded inside Item 10's own body, alongside Item 10's substantial inline content (executive officer bios, Code of Conduct, Insider Trading Policy). Items 11 and 13 then read only the one-line internal cross-reference 'Refer to Item 10.' (18 chars); Item 12 reads 'Refer to Item 10 for security ownership ...' plus its own equity-compensation-plan table; Item 14 reads 'Refer to Item 10.' All four are classified 'extracted' here, not 'incorporated_by_reference' -- the rule applied is: a pointer to another ITEM WITHIN THIS SAME FILING is extracted (the text is genuinely present, however short); 'incorporated_by_reference' is reserved for a pointer to an EXTERNAL document (proxy statement, prior filing, annual report exhibit), which is how AAPL/MSFT/GE/Textron's Part III items were classified. This interpretive call is now RATIFIED by specs/decisions/ADR-004-pointer-item-status.md (shape 2, 'internal same-document pointer' -- JPM Items 7 and 8 are its canonical examples in the ADR itself), not left as an open judgment call.
